To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
affective reactions to alternatives in choice tasks are more likely to influence choice when the availability of resources for cognitive processing is limited.

affective reactions and cognitive evaluations of the alternatives are both important determinants of choice, that affective reactions tend to dominate cognitive evaluations if processing resources are low, and that cognitive evaluations tend to dominate affective reactions if processing resources are high.

affective reactions and cognitions can have opposite effects on choice, and that affective reactions tend to be stronger than cognitions in influencing choice when the consumer is under time pressure, when the consumer is presented with the alternatives in a more passive way (i.e., by reading about them), and when the consumer has low levels of impulsivity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of affect in consumer decision making.
the interplay between affective and cognitive factors in the decision making process.
the interplay between affect and cognition in consumer decision making.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the affect and cognitions are in conflict in consumer decision making, and this conflict is resolved by the availability of the processing resources.
affective and cognitive factors are not mutually exclusive, but rather they are complementary.
affective reactions and cognitions play an important and interdependent role in consumer decision making.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the affective and cognitive reactions to alternatives are processed differently.
the affective reactions that are spontaneously evoked in the choice context have a stronger influence on choice than do cognitions when processing resources are limited.
the heart and the mind are not always in agreement.
The main takeaway from our work is that
affect and cognition can be in conflict.
affect and cognition can have opposite impacts on decision making.
when people are making choices, they are influenced by two things: their emotions and their thoughts.
